scores.accuracy_concern: Confirm from the full text whether 18% is the share of the whole sample living alone or the share of lonely people who lived alone before pairing it with 43%; do not use mortality prediction to rank loneliness above living alone, since in ELSA (Steptoe 2013) isolation, not loneliness, stayed linked with death after adjustment.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the paper's own cross-tabulation of lonely people by living arrangement and print the three short-scale questions verbatim on the card.

scores.values_concern: Frame a care home move as sometimes the right outcome; the post should question premature decisions, not imply that a care home is a failure.
scores.accuracy_concern: The free minor adaptations rule (up to 1,000 pounds, England) is in the Care and Support (Preventing Needs for Care and Support) Regulations 2014, not the charging regulations cited; the NHS discharge guidance wording must be verified from a copy; the 46% and 57% Scottish figures come from different periods and definitions, so use one.
scores.sharpen: Cut to one Scottish figure, add the question 'Can we try home with this support and review it in a few weeks?', and say plainly that a care home can be the right answer when the named problems cannot be solved.

scores.accuracy_concern: The lag of up to 23 days describes delayed deaths after exposure on the cold day, not continuing risk from indoor temperature in the following weeks, so 'keep warm for the weeks after' does not follow from the study; the Keatinge cooling study used young volunteers and cannot sit on an older-person timeline as if it were about them.
scores.sharpen: Rewrite the position around the delay (deaths linked with one cold day continue for up to three weeks, so watch for chest and heart symptoms afterwards) and drop the young-volunteer laboratory study.

scores.accuracy_concern: Verify the sex-specific estimates (a women's RR of 1.04 with CI 1.00 to 1.08 is borderline and should be called small rather than absent); relative risks need a plain framing in words, and loss of practical care as the mechanism is a hypothesis, not a finding.
scores.sharpen: Describe the risk in words rather than as RR labels on the visual, and make the checklist (who now does the meals, medicines, money, driving and appointments) the centrepiece.

scores.accuracy_concern: Do not turn OR 1.91 into 'twice as likely'; the pooled studies are observational and people often stop driving because their health is already declining, so the links with depression and care home admission may reflect the reason for stopping.
scores.sharpen: Open with the practical question 'How will you get to the shop, your friends and the GP?' and add one verified UK transport option such as concessionary travel or community transport.

scores.values_concern: Risk of minimising loneliness in the oldest and housebound people, who are least represented in online surveys.
scores.accuracy_concern: The BBC Loneliness Experiment is a self-selected online sample, so its older respondents are unlikely to represent housebound or offline older people; UK studies suggest loneliness rises again in the oldest age groups, which the post must state rather than leave unresolved.
scores.sharpen: Replace the online survey with a representative UK source, state that loneliness rises again in the oldest groups, and make the ask 'find people by circumstances such as bereavement, poor health and living alone'.

scores.accuracy_concern: Schulz 2004 is a US study of dementia carers; the England home and pension disregard rules (half of an occupational or personal pension passed to a spouse at home) must be verified from the statutory guidance, and Scottish rules stated separately or omitted.
scores.sharpen: Keep the money points as questions to ask the council's financial assessment team unless the statutory guidance is verified, and name that team as the place to ask.

scores.accuracy_concern: Form names, the 12-month threshold and its dates (April 2022 for Universal Credit and ESA, April 2023 for PIP, DLA and Attendance Allowance) and the Scottish BASRiS criteria all rest on official pages that could not be opened; the Marie Curie poverty figure is unsourced and should be cut.
scores.sharpen: Hold until the DWP and Social Security Scotland guidance can be verified from an opened copy, then lead with the outdated six-month belief and keep the two-column card.

scores.accuracy_concern: Home oxygen electricity reimbursement applies to concentrators through the home oxygen supplier and may differ in Scotland; dialysis reimbursement varies by unit; a stairlift is not medical equipment in the same sense and air mattress running costs are unverified, so the opening line groups unlike items.
scores.sharpen: Narrow to home oxygen and the Priority Services Register, the two points most likely to verify, and drop the stairlift and mattress examples.

scores.accuracy_concern: In Peel 2005 physical function and performance explained most of the variance in life-space, with sociodemographic factors adding 13%, so the claim that life-space picks up transport, money and confidence is plausible rather than shown; the mortality link is observational.
scores.sharpen: Give one life-space question a clinician can ask in clinic, and present 'a shrinking life-space should prompt questions about pain, confidence, transport and money' as a clinical judgement; check fit against C02.

scores.accuracy_concern: All key claims rest on NHS England proxy-access guidance that could not be opened; arrangements in Scotland and Wales differ; proxy access for a person who lacks capacity has specific conditions that must not be simplified.
scores.sharpen: Verify from an opened copy of the guidance, add a one-line Scotland and Wales caveat, and open with the security problem of logging in with a parent's password.

scores.accuracy_concern: Next of kin gives no decision-making authority for adults in UK healthcare, but Scotland's Adults with Incapacity Act 'nearest relative' and mental health 'named person' roles exist, so 'no legal role' is too broad; the Stonewall 2011 figures are unverified.
scores.sharpen: Add one line on Scotland's 'nearest relative' role and end on two concrete actions: tell the ward who you want contacted, and arrange a power of attorney while you are able to.

scores.values_concern: The commissioning argument approaches a policy position; keep it to the Care Act wording and the NICE standard and avoid implying blame of commissioners or providers.
scores.accuracy_concern: The claim that visits are often too short for company needs a published source on time-and-task commissioning; the NICE NG21 wording on visits under 30 minutes must be quoted exactly and applies to England only.
scores.sharpen: Find a published source on time-and-task commissioning, quote the Care Act wording beside the NICE 30-minute standard, and keep care workers explicitly outside the criticism; check fit against C16.

scores.accuracy_concern: Linked entitlements changed in 2024 and 2025 (Winter Fuel Payment rules; Scotland's Pension Age Winter Heating Payment), the take-up figure is unverified, and every claim relies on DWP pages that could not be opened.
scores.sharpen: Verify the linked entitlements for the posting year and the DWP take-up estimate, and lead with the one linked form of help most likely to be worth more than a small award.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 2010 comparison was with smoking fewer than 15 cigarettes a day and used a composite of social relationship measures, not loneliness; the 2015 meta-analysis did find loneliness linked with mortality in adjusted studies (OR 1.26), so the ELSA result must sit beside it rather than stand as the answer.
scores.sharpen: Show the three findings side by side in plain words (2010 composite of social relationships, 2015 loneliness after adjustment, ELSA loneliness not independent) and close with the reason to act that needs no slogan: loneliness is distressing.

scores.accuracy_concern: The change was modest (1.1 points on a 3 to 9 scale), one of two loneliness scales did not show a clear difference, follow-up was 4 weeks during the pandemic and 37% of participants were under 65; the 'same caller' and 'person leads' features must be confirmed in the full text before they appear on the visual.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the young callers and the call schedule, state the 4-week limit and the modest size of the change in plain words, and name what a befriending service could copy.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 14 studies covered adults of all ages, not older people specifically, and the 27 pounds per 1 pound social return is a modelled estimate built on low-quality studies; omit it or label it as modelled.
scores.sharpen: Say that the studies included all ages, and give one concrete referral route (council welfare rights or a Citizens Advice service in the practice) instead of the modelled return.

scores.accuracy_concern: Rates, the 6-month qualifying rule and the Pension Age Disability Payment rollout dates in Scotland must be verified from official sources that could not be opened; receiving Attendance Allowance raises Pension Credit entitlement only for some people.
scores.sharpen: Verify the current rates and the Scottish rollout from an opened source, and end with how to start a claim so the post closes on an action.

scores.accuracy_concern: Lindau data are from 2005 to 2006 in the US; 26% of people aged 75 to 85 were sexually active, so 'many' should be 'about 1 in 4'; the medicine side-effect claim needs a named source such as the BNF.
scores.sharpen: Use natural frequencies ('about 1 in 4 people aged 75 to 85'), cite a named source for the medicines, and give the exact wording of one opening question for clinic.

scores.values_concern: Arguing for help 'whatever income' could read as diluting priority for people in fuel poverty; keep the poorest explicit.
scores.accuracy_concern: Healy 2003 is an ecological comparison of countries in the 1990s, so 'housing counts more than climate' is an association between countries, not a measure of individual risk; Wilkinson found little variation by deprivation in people aged 75 and over, which is not evidence that fuel poverty has no effect.
scores.sharpen: Describe Healy as a comparison of countries in the 1990s and turn the insight into actions (heat the room you sit in; ask about insulation and draught-proofing help); choose this or C17-03, not both.

scores.values_concern: Criticise the label and the system, not emergency or acute staff.
scores.accuracy_concern: One Canadian centre with 60 labelled patients; the 88% and delay figures must be matched to the full text; HR 3.06 for missed diagnosis and 180-day death is an association in a trauma cohort and must not become 'three times more likely to die'.
scores.sharpen: Show the 60-person icon array, add one line naming the commonest missed diagnoses from the full text without singling out delirium, and check fit against C15.

scores.values_concern: A missed appointment can be an informed choice; contact should seek the reason and respect a decision not to attend, and 'was not brought' safeguarding language should not be applied to adults who can decide for themselves.
scores.accuracy_concern: RRR values come from a multinomial model against reference groups that must be confirmed, and adults aged 16 to 30 were also at high risk, so older age should not be presented as unique; the mortality link is a risk marker, not a cause.
scores.sharpen: Mention young adults as the other high-risk group, make the close 'phone before you discharge', and add one line respecting a person's choice not to attend.

scores.values_concern: Close to a policy position on digital-first services; keep it to fair access and a measurable standard.
scores.accuracy_concern: The central statistic (people aged 75 and over least likely to use the internet) and the NHS digital inclusion framework rely on Ofcom, ONS and NHS pages that were not opened; a peer-reviewed source is needed before use.
scores.sharpen: Find a peer-reviewed or opened official source for the internet-use figure and propose one measurable standard, such as time to book by phone compared with online.

scores.values_concern: Frame the daily check as company and practical help, not surveillance of people who live alone.
scores.accuracy_concern: In Semenza 1996 the highest odds were for being confined to bed and not leaving home each day; living alone had a smaller odds ratio, so 'among the strongest' overstates it; both studies date from 1995 and 2003, and air conditioning findings do not transfer directly to UK homes.
scores.sharpen: Order the risk factors by the study's own odds ratios, add one UK-relevant practical step (curtains closed on the sunny side, water within reach, a cooler room downstairs), and schedule for early summer.

scores.values_concern: Avoid presenting lesbian, gay and bisexual older people as a problem group; the point is that the form should fit everyone.
scores.accuracy_concern: The Stonewall 2011 findings and the claim that LGB older people rely more on services are unverified; the CQC 2019 guidance title and content need checking.
scores.sharpen: Anchor the post in one verified source on older people without a partner or children, and show where the two questions belong on a real admission or care home form; pair or merge with C17-12 rather than running both close together.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 2017 review is nine years old and needs a recent systematic review beside it; Masi 2011's finding on social cognition rests on few trials and later reviews are less clear; neither review is specific to older people.
scores.sharpen: Add a post-2020 systematic review and give link workers one concrete outcome to record, such as a short loneliness scale before and after referral.

scores.accuracy_concern: Participants were of all ages in low-income households, so any older-person effect needs the full-text age breakdown; the crude comparison (relative rate 0.86, CI 0.66 to 1.12) did not show a clear difference and must be stated as plainly as the adjusted 26%.
scores.sharpen: Give both results side by side as injuries per 100 people per year, state the trial population in the first sentence, and check fit against C01 and E068.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 2024 Lancet Commission report has not yet been read; the Whitehall II association (HR 0.88 per SD) was for contact with friends and is observational; the reverse-causation wording must be taken from the paper itself.
scores.sharpen: Name exactly what to check (mood, a hearing test, a memory history from someone who knows the person) and read the Lancet Commission report before quoting it; keep clear of earlier dementia and hearing posts (E005, E006, E019).

allocation_reason: 26 of 28 candidates reach 36 or more with no disqualifying flag and 15 reach 42 or more, most with low evidence risk, so the category supports the top of the range even if C17-21, C17-27 and C17-10 are ceded to C15, C01 and C02.
balance_note: The top 14 by score are 8 practitioner, 2 both and 4 public posts, and pensioner poverty is thin (only C17-17 and the money questions in C17-07); swap one or two of the cross-category practitioner items (C17-10, C17-27 or C17-21) for C17-05 (both, transport) and a verified public money post (C17-18), and run only one of the cold-weather pair (C17-03 or C17-20) alongside the heat post C17-24.
